region.text: Mystras and the Laconian core, Monemvasia, Grand Magne (Mani) and Karytaina with the eastern half of its barony: the nucleus of the Despotate

ledger.note: 1349: John VI Kantakouzenos creates the Despotate of the Morea at Mystras for his son Manuel. The Despotate page: established 1349 'as an appanage for his son Manuel'; infobox capital 'Mystras 1349-1460'. The Manuel page has him arrive in the province on 25 October 1349 and calls him the first of the long-ruling despots. The nucleus is the 1262 cession of Mystras, Monemvasia and the Grand Magne (Mystras page); neither page gives a boundary. Region revised 2026-10-19 to the named nucleus (see the first keyframe).

1388: Despot Theodore I Palaiologos takes Argos. The Lordship page: 'Despot Theodore Palaiologos took Argos with Nerio Acciaioli and an Ottoman army'; 'Argos, Kiveri and Thermisi remained in Theodore's hands until 11 June 1394'. Maria of Enghien had sold the lordship to Venice on 12 December 1388; Venice secured Nauplia only.
11 June 1394: Theodore cedes Argos, Kiveri and Thermisi to Venice, which keeps them (the Despotate page lists the Argolid and Nafplion among what Venice 'kept' to 1461).

About 1402: Salona 'fell for a short time into the hands of the Despotate of the Morea' (Lordship of Salona page). The page names no month and no previous holder after the Ottoman entry of 1394; the Ottomans are the researcher's reading.
1404: Theodore I sells Salona to the Hospitallers. 'Despot Theodore I Palaiologos sold Salona to the Knights Hospitaller in 1404' (Lordship of Salona page).

region.text: Messenia and Elis, invaded in 1417 by Theodore II Palaeologus and John VIII

ledger.note: 1417: Theodore II and John VIII invade Achaea. The Centurione page: in 1417 an imperial army 'led by Theodore II Palaeologus and Emperor John VIII' invaded Achaea and took Messenia and Elis; no month.

1418: the campaign ends. The page has Centurione 'holed up' in Glarentza and fleeing it by sea 'in the spring of 1418'; Olivier Franco seized Glarentza the same year. The page does not date the end of the fighting more exactly.

union.text: the barony of Arcadia (Kyparissia), Achaean until 1432

region.text: Messenia and Elis, without the Venetian ports of Modon, Coron and Navarino and without Kyparissia (Achaean to 1432)

ledger.note: 1418: the Despotate holds Messenia and Elis. The Centurione page dates the taking of both to the 1417 campaign; 1418 is when Centurione fled, and the eu-05-d Achaea dossier's loss event uses 1418. Region revised 2026-10-19: Navarino and Kyparissia subtracted (Venetian from 1417; gained in 1432).

region.text: the rest of the Latin Morea: the peninsula without the Venetian ports and Argolid, without Kyparissia (gained 1432) and without Patras (Venetian, next event)

ledger.note: 1430: the Despotate takes the rest of the Latin Morea. The page: 'expanded to cover the entire peninsula' in 1430 'through dowry settlements and Constantine's conquest of Patras'; the Centurione page has Thomas force a treaty (1429/1430) by which he married Catherine at Mystras in 1430 and became heir, Centurione retiring to Arcadia. The year is the page's; the exact line is the researcher's reading. Region revised 2026-10-19: Patras removed (the Patras page makes it Venetian from 1408), Navarino and Kyparissia carved out.

1430: the Despotate takes Patras from Venice. Patras page: 'In 1408, Patras became Venetian'; Venetian rule ended when the city was recaptured in 1430 by the Despotate of Morea under Constantine Palaiologos. The Despotate page names 'Constantine's conquest of Patras' without a year; the Achaea dossier's 1430 loss gives Patras to the empire as an Achaean loss, which the Patras page does not support.

region.text: the barony of Arcadia (Kyparissia), Centurione's last lands: 'He died there two years later in 1432. His domains passed to the despotate of Morea'

ledger.note: 1432: Centurione II Zaccaria dies in Arcadia and his last barony passes to the Despotate. The Thomas page agrees: Thomas gained Achaean lands through his marriage 'after Centurione's death in 1432'. The Centurione page's infobox puts the principality's end at 1430.

region.text: Athens, the Acciaioli duchy of Attica and Boeotia

ledger.note: 1444: Athens becomes a tributary of the Despot of the Morea. 'In 1444 Athens became a tributary of Constantine Palaeologus, the Despot of Morea and heir to the Byzantine throne' (Duchy of Athens page). The page does not say what Constantine received or whether the Ottomans were also paid.

region.text: the remnants of the Duchy of Athens

ledger.note: 1456: the Ottomans end the duchy's tribute to the Morea. The Duchy page: 'Turahanoglu Omer Bey conquered the remnants of the Duchy' in 1456 after the fall of Constantinople; the Acropolis held to June 1458. Bridging for the end of the Morea's suzerainty: the page does not mention the Despotate in 1456.

1458: Mehmed II annexes the north of the Morea. The page: Mehmed 'marched into the Morea in May' 1458, Corinth surrendered in August, 'Corinth, Patras, and the northwest were annexed', the brothers keeping the south under tribute. The Despotate page is silent on 1458. Month 8 is Corinth's surrender.

region.text: the south: Mystras and the remaining Despotate

ledger.note: 1460: Mystras falls to Mehmed II. The Despotate page: Ottoman conquest of Mystras on 29 May 1460, Demetrios a prisoner, Thomas fled; 'By the end of summer, virtually all Greek cities had submitted'. The Mystras page gives 30 and 31 May.

region.text: after Mehmed II's 1458 campaign 'Corinth, Patras, and the northwest were annexed, and the brothers kept the south under tribute'

ledger.note: 1460: the Despotate of the Morea ends. Mehmed II takes Mystras (29 May) and the rest of the Morea by summer; Monemvasia is under papal protection from late 1460 and Salmenikon holds out until July 1461 ('the end of the Byzantine Empire proper'); Venice keeps Modon, Koroni, the Argolid and Nafplion.

wars.name: Byzantine conquest of the Principality of Achaea
wars.outcome: Theodore II and John VIII took Messenia and Elis in 1417-18; Thomas besieged Centurione at Chalandritsa in 1429 and forced the treaty and marriage of 1429/1430; Centurione died in Arcadia in 1432 and the Despotate took his lands.
wars.note: Constantine's capture of Patras is on the Despotate page for 1430 and undated on the Thomas page. Zone revised 2026-10-19 to exclude the Venetian ports; the Patras page makes Patras a Venetian city from 1408 until the Despotate took it in 1430 (ledger).

wars.name: Manuel Kantakouzenos's war with Francesco Sansverino at Gardiki
wars.outcome: Manuel's army of about 1,000 knights and 2,000 infantry was defeated by Sansverino, the bailli of Achaea, in the mid-1370s; no territory changed hands.
wars.note: The page says 'mid-1370s' for the Gardiki conflict; the years here are the researcher's bracket.

wars.name: Ottoman invasion of the Morea of 1446

zones.text: the Hexamilion at the Isthmus of Corinth

wars.outcome: Murad II destroyed the Hexamilion wall; Thomas and Constantine 'accepted Murad as lord, agreed to pay tribute, and promised not to rebuild the wall'. No land changed hands.
wars.note: The Thomas page dates Turahan Bey's demolition of the Hexamilion to 1431; the Despotate page has Murad destroying it in 1446. The Ottoman dossier (me-10) should carry the tributary relation.

wars.name: Albanian-Greek revolt of 1453-54
wars.outcome: The Albanian and Greek revolt after the fall of Constantinople was put down in October 1454 with Turahan Bey's Ottoman troops, whom the despots had invited; the tribute rose from 10,000 to 12,000 ducats.
wars.note: The Despotate page gives 1453-1454 and the Ottoman troops; the Thomas page gives December 1453 and October 1454.

wars.name: Ottoman conquest of the Morea

zones.text: Corinth, Patras, the northwest, then the south

wars.outcome: Mehmed II annexed Corinth, Patras and the northwest in 1458 (the brothers having paid no tribute for three years); Thomas rebelled against Demetrios and the Ottomans in January 1459; Demetrios surrendered Mystras without a fight on 29 May 1460.
wars.note: Thomas fled to Methoni and Corfu (22 July 1460) and sailed for Italy on 16 November 1460.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey line is on any page opened: the Latin-Byzantine frontier with Achaea, the Ottoman marches and the borders between the co-despots are approximate. The Venetian enclaves of Modon, Koroni, Navarino and the Argolid (Argos and Nauplia) are the sharp exceptions (fixed fortified ports), carved out of the shapes as coastal circles; the nucleus of 1349-1417 is a lower bound.

notes:
Written by eu-05-x (additions). Cliopatria has no row; slug free. Five pages opened for the core (the budget), three more (Duchy of Athens, Lordship of Argos and Nauplia, Lordship of Salona) for the vassal, Argos and Salona events. Not settled: (1) no page opened gives the Despotate's area or the extent of the Byzantine Morea between 1349 and 1417: Karytaina (1320), Mani, Geraki, the Skorta barony, and the Pelagonia date (1259 on the Despotate page, 1262 for the handover) need the Principality of Achaea and Byzantine Morea pages; (2) the dates of Corinth's and Patras's entry (Despot Theodore I and Hexamilion 1415, Patras 1429-30) are not on pages opened; (3) Argos, Kiveri and Thermisi are Theodore I's only from 1388 to 11 June 1394 (Lordship of Argos and Nauplia page; ledger events), a detail the 1349-1416 keyframe does not draw; Nauplia was never Despotate land; (4) the Ottoman tributary relation from 1446 is recorded in wars only (the ledger's vassal events belong to the suzerain's dossier); (5) type is 'colony' (an appanage drawn in the Byzantine Empire's tint), but from 1453 the Despotate was the empire's only remnant and might be drawn as a state. Names not in the gazetteer: Kyparissia, Nauplia/Argos (coordinates used).

Revision 2026-10-19 (eu-05-x repair after review 'fail'): (a) the 1349-1417 shape was a 75 km Sparti circle that overlapped Venetian Coron, Modon and Navarino, the Argolid and Achaean Messenia; it is now the named nucleus (Sparti 30 km, Monemvasia 25 km, Mani 30 km, Karytaina 20 km), split into keyframes 1349, 1388 (+ Argos, Kiveri, Thermisi), 1394, 1402 (+ Salona) and 1404 so that the ledger's gains and losses of 1388, 1394, 1402 and 1404 are all drawn; (b) the 1418, 1430 and 1458 shapes now carve out Navarino; 1418 and 1458 carve out the Argolid (1418 no longer contains it); 1418 and 1430-31 carve out Kyparissia (the 1430 shape is split at 1432); (c) Patras came from Venice in 1430 (Patras page), so a gain event from republic-of-venice was added and Patras removed from the Achaea gain; (d) Modon and Coron circles now use the venetian-modon-and-coron dossier's own coordinates and 15 km. Opened again: Hexamilion wall (silent on the holder of the Isthmus and on Corinth), Despotate of the Morea (silent on 1349-1417 extent and on when Corinth passed), Theodore I Palaiologos, Barony of Karytaina, Principality of Achaea, Patras; Corinth (disambiguation page, no content). Left undrawn because no page gives a start of holding: Geraki, Skorta, Corinth before 1430 (the Theodore I page has it bought 1395/6 and sold to the Hospitallers in 1397; the despotate sold to the Hospitallers 1399-1400 and regained 1404 - transfers the Hospitaller dossier does not carry), Glarentza from 1 May 1428 (byzantine-empire ledger only). Not changed: the counterpart convention for the 1418, 1430 and 1432 gains (colony versus metropole), left to the orchestrator.
